Description: Detected a potential hardcoded password literal, which may expose account credentials.

Attributes.git.message:
S5b.1: harden GraphGuard's runtime -- Redis, Postgres, MLflow, the scorer pod

- Safety net first: every GraphGuard database dumped and restored once into a
  throwaway container; row counts identical.
- Redis: current 7.4 patch by digest; one user per client with only the
  commands it uses (serving/redis_acl.py), default user off, no scripting or
  admin for anyone, hashes-only ACL file; scorer credentials from a Kubernetes
  Secret; non-root (not a uid that belongs to another app on the host),
  read-only, no capabilities.
- Postgres: current 16.x patch by digest; pg_hba generated from
  ops/pg_access.py (own role + own DB, SCRAM, reject the rest, superuser local
  only); MLflow on its own role, password via PGPASSFILE, superuser rotated.
- MLflow: no credential in its command line; 2 workers (private memory 730 ->
  426 MiB idle).
- Every compose service held to one standard by tests/test_compose_hardening.py.
- Scorer pod: Pod Security restricted enforced on the namespace, non-root,
  read-only root, no SA token, egress denied except DNS, Redis and Ray. The
  egress test caught that Docker DNATs 10.42.0.1:6380 to the container before
  the policy is checked; the rule allows the real destination.
- Memory caps re-sized from measured peaks: sum 4.0 GiB.
- Verified: 2,000/2,000 scores identical after every step, p99 10.9 ms on k3s,
  465 tests, clean copy under a 2 GB cap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
